skill.name: starknet-js
skill.description: Reference for building Starknet applications with starknet.js v9, including provider setup, accounts, contracts, transactions, fees, wallets, and paymasters.
skill.summary: Build Starknet integrations with practical starknet.js v9 patterns.
skill.author: internet-court

security_audit.summary: AI review confirmed six static findings in scripts/account-example.ts related to environment access and raw Starknet private-key handling. The remaining static findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, documentation URLs, reference links, or normal Starknet API examples, and no prompt injection was found. One semantic finding notes overbroad tool permissions in the skill metadata.

remediation.suggestion: Use a testnet-only signer example, prefer wallet or external signer integrations, and warn users not to expose production keys.

remediation.issue: Skill metadata grants broad tools for a reference skill.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to read-only lookup tools unless a workflow truly needs Bash, Write, or Task.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples mention private-key generation and signer wiring without enough storage guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Add clear guidance to use secure key storage, avoid committed secrets, and separate development keys from production accounts.

remediation.issue: Examples include hardcoded public RPC and paymaster endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: State that production users should configure trusted endpoints per environment and review third-party provider terms.

This is a TypeScript template literal inside throw new Error, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. It formats an error message and does not invoke a command interpreter.

The helper reads named environment variables and is used by this script to load RPC, account, and private-key values. Environment access is intentional, but it touches signing credentials, so it remains a real low-severity secret-handling risk.
The script accesses process.env and later uses that path to retrieve STARKNET_PRIVATE_KEY. This is expected for a sample script, but it is still real secret-bearing environment access.
The run instructions ask users to provide STARKNET_PRIVATE_KEY to a runnable command. A Starknet private key controls signing authority, so disclosure or reuse can compromise funds.
The script explicitly loads STARKNET_PRIVATE_KEY into memory for account signing. This is legitimate Starknet usage, but raw private-key handling is a real high-impact secret risk.
The code reads process.env at runtime and does not open a .env file or access the filesystem. The actual private-key handling is covered by the separate confirmed findings.
Line 20 retrieves the private key that will authorize Starknet account actions. The code does not exfiltrate it, but requiring a raw private key in a sample is a real credential-handling risk.
The private key is passed directly as the Account signer, granting transaction authority to the process. Any compromise of the runtime environment would expose signing capability.

content.value_statement: Starknet integrations need precise provider, account, transaction, and fee handling. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical starknet.js v9 patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to create RpcProvider connections for mainnet and Sepolia.
Explains account creation, deployment, and connection to existing accounts.
Provides contract read, write, typed contract, event, and multicall patterns.
Covers transaction simulation, fee estimation, custom resource bounds, and receipt handling.
Includes wallet connection, paymaster, SNIP-9, SNIP-12, and Cairo type examples.
limitations: Does not teach Cairo contract authoring or formal contract security review.
Uses examples that require users to choose trusted RPC and paymaster providers.
Includes private-key examples that need secure signer and storage practices.
May need updates when starknet.js or Starknet RPC versions change.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Starknet dApp
use_cases.description: Plan provider setup, contract calls, typed ABI use, and wallet connection for a frontend integration.

use_cases.title: Build Transaction Services
use_cases.description: Design backend flows for account execution, fee estimation, simulation, receipts, and nonce-aware operations.

use_cases.title: Add Sponsored Transactions
use_cases.description: Evaluate paymaster flows, sponsored mode, alternate gas tokens, and policy checks before submitting transactions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Provider Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for reading Starknet data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a starknet.js v9 provider setup for Sepolia. Include chain checks and basic read-only contract access.

prompt_templates.title: Connect an Account
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a safe starknet.js account connection flow. Include signer boundaries, fee estimation, and transaction receipt handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multicall Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced contract interaction with batched calls.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a starknet.js multicall that approves a token and deposits into a contract. Include simulation and resource bounds.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Paymaster Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a Starknet paymaster integration. Check sponsor policy, supported tokens, fee estimates, and failure handling.

output_examples.input: I need to read an ERC-20 balance from Starknet Sepolia.
output_examples.output: A provider setup plan, contract connection steps, ABI requirements, and a note to keep token amounts as BigInt values.

output_examples.input: I want to send a sponsored transaction through a paymaster.
output_examples.output: A flow covering paymaster setup, supported token discovery, fee estimation, sponsor approval, execution, and receipt checks.

output_examples.input: My transaction sometimes fails after simulation.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist for nonce refresh, RPC consistency, resource bounds, fee drift, and revert reason handling.

best_practices: Simulate transactions and estimate fees before submitting account executions.
Use BigInt for token amounts, balances, and fee values to avoid precision loss.
Keep signer credentials separate from application configuration and logs.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production private keys into examples, prompts, logs, or committed files.
Do not rely on implicit RPC defaults for production Starknet environments.
Do not retry deterministic validation or calldata errors as transient network failures.

faq.question: Does this skill support starknet.js v9?
faq.answer: Yes. The references target starknet.js v9 patterns for providers, accounts, contracts, transactions, wallets, and paymasters.

faq.question: Can it write Cairo smart contracts?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on TypeScript integration with deployed Starknet contracts, not Cairo contract development.

faq.question: Does it perform a security audit?
faq.answer: No. It offers implementation guidance and operational guardrails, but formal contract or wallet security review is out of scope.

faq.question: Can it help with fee estimation?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers invoke fee estimates, resource bounds, priority tips, and sponsored transaction fee flows.

faq.question: Does it require a private key?
faq.answer: Read-only provider tasks do not need a private key. Transaction signing needs a secure wallet, signer, or development-only key.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
